children: Abu Dhabi-based Mubadala Investment Co. is investing in one of China's largest coffee chains in a transaction valued at about $1 billion.
The sovereign investor is making the minority investment in Luckin Coffee alongside China-focused private-equity firm Centurium Capital, Luckin's controlling shareholder.
The move comes as Chinese consumers drink more coffee more frequently, spurring growth in the market, the firms said Thursday.
"We continue to see compelling long-term opportunities in China's consumer sector," said Mohamed Albadr, head of Asia, private equity, at Mubadala.
Mubadala, whose $385 billion portfolio spans six continents, first entered China in 2015.
Since then, it has deployed over $20 billion across more than 100 investments in the country in multiple sectors and asset classes.

Founded in 2017, Xiamen-based Luckin has made a name for itself with an app-centric strategy and competitive pricing. It operates about 36,000 stores worldwide. As of end-June, its transacting customer tally stood at close to half a billion.
